correctness.rationale: The prescribed compact vector solves the hub cancellation on each of its three incident hubs. Its translates have Gram symbol 1+cos(phi/2) cos(k)>0 and span the one-dimensional flat fiber. The decaying root of the Gram recurrence is -r and the n=0 equation fixes the inverse normalization (1+r²)/(1-r²). For d≥2 the four touched translates are distinct; the restricted onsite Gram is two copies of a block with eigenvalues (1±r)²/[2(1+r²)]>0. Thus the Hermitian reduction is positive definite and rank four. In the symmetric/antisymmetric basis its same-cell blocks are diag((1+r)/2,(1-r)/2); the intercell Gram kernel before the change of basis is proportional to [[-r,r²],[1,-r]], yielding the stated rank-one off-block with entries of magnitude h_d after whitening. In a shifted spectral variable y=x-1/2, the rank-one Schur determinant multiplies (y²-r²/4)² by 1-h_d²[2y/(y²-r²/4)]². Hence the four roots are positive and distinct and the two ordered doublets split by precisely 2h_d. For the full operator, ker(H0)∩ker(W_d) remains a reducing zero subspace and its orthogonal complement has a four-dimensional isolated zero eigenspace separated from the dispersive spectrum by the fixed positive gap. Ordinary isolated-cluster perturbation on that complement gives slopes equal to the four compression eigenvalues, hence the claimed O(epsilon²) expansions at fixed J, phi, d. At phi=pi/2, r=sqrt(2)-1 and the ratio is r². No finite-strength equality or uniform estimate in closing gap or increasing d is certified.

value.rationale: The exact invariant answers a comparison already singled out in a physical model: whether two channels merely appear close, and what sets the distance dependence of their effective tunneling. It gives a usable normalization and a sharp separation law for the weak-impurity regime, while distinguishing a true projection identity from the full-Hamiltonian approximation.
residual_risks: No claim is made about transport, topological protection or finite-strength equality.
